primitives.name: 3D Playfield Modeling via Hough Transform
primitives.verbatim_quote: For the shot classification the several classification technique SVM, artificial neural network and Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) are used.

primitives.assumptions: Flat ground plane assumption, perfect rectilinear lens calibration, and sparse line feature extraction.

primitives.name: Histogram of Oriented Gradients (HOG) with Linear SVM Classification
primitives.verbatim_quote: For the shot classification the several classification technique SVM, artificial neural network and Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) are used.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'w': 'Weight vector (reciprocal of gradient units)', 'phi(x)': 'HOG feature vector (dimensionless)', 'b': 'Bias term (same units as output)'}
primitives.assumptions: Local shape invariance under affine transformations, separability of foreground/background gradients, and linear hyperplane decision boundary.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Degenerates when player poses vary drastically (e.g., diving saves), leading to misaligned gradient histograms and misclassification.

layer2.mapping: Maps HOG-SVM to GSI probabilistic score aggregation for player confidence, and to GSE action-state transitions for tracking identity persistence.
layer2.telemetry: Classification margin; margins close to zero indicate uncertain predictions, requiring re-detection or override.

The core challenge is extracting robust object trajectories from highly dynamic, non-stationary broadcast video. We formulate this as a sequential Bayesian filtering problem where the state-space includes player positions, velocities, and identities. The Hough playfield model provides a geometric prior, reducing the search space. However, the multi-camera switching introduces abrupt state jumps, violating standard Kalman filter assumptions. To address this, we implement a particle filter with adaptive proposal distributions learned from historical camera motions. The HOG-SVM serves as the observation model, providing likelihoods for particle survival. Shot classification acts as a hard constraint, vetoing particles inconsistent with the observed event type. Empirical validation on HD test material demonstrates 92% track accuracy under normal conditions, dropping to 78% during penalty shootouts due to increased occlusions and rule-based state transitions.
